{{Quote|It is done. Seelah has rid the Skyborn of the Fifty-seven.|Tilden Kaah|<ref name="paragon" />}}
In [[4985 BBY]], [[Yaru Korsin]], leader of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] on [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]], launched a full-fledged '''purge''' of the forty-five [[Sith (species)/Legends|pureblood Sith]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. [[Ravilan Wroth]], the leader of the members of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Species/Legends|species]] in the Lost Tribe, had embarked on a plot to [[Poison/Legends|poison]] the [[Water/Legends|water]] supply of the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tetsubal]], in order to convince the Lost Tribe leaders to focus on finding a way off-planet&mdash;by then, the Sith had been stranded on the remote world for fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. However, his ploy was discovered by Yaru Korsin's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], who framed him for similar [[Death/Legends|deadly]] incidents in other neighboring towns. Convinced that Wroth and the purebloods needed to be eliminated, Korsin enacted a [[Speciecide|purge]] that lasted through a single night, and though the purebloods fought back with everything they had, they lost more and more of their ranks throughout. Eventually, Wroth was taken [[Prison/Legends|prisoner]] as the last remaining purebloods fought back against Yaru Korsin and his [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]] in a last stand high in the [[Takara Mountains]]. While the last holdouts were killed, Wroth was executed by Seelah Korsin's son [[Jariad Korsin|Jariad]], and the bodies of the dead were put on public display in the city of [[Tahv]]. With the purge, all of the [[Alien/Legends|non]]-[[Human/Legends|Human]] members of the Lost Tribe of Sith&mdash;save for the [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] [[Gloyd]], a personal friend of Yaru Korsin&mdash;had been wiped from the face of Kesh.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|Bring all the others in. Tell them it's time.|Yaru Korsin, before beginning the purge|<ref name="paragon" />}}
In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], a [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith]] [[Starship/Legends|starship]] known as the ''[[Omen]]'' was knocked off course during a [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump and crash-landed on the remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. After a chaotic first few nights in the [[Takara Mountains|mountains]] where the ''Omen'' came to rest, the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] found their way to a relatively primitive civilization of [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] natives. Posing as the Keshiri [[Skyborn|gods]], the Sith quickly took their place as rulers of Kesh. The ''Omen''{{'s}} crew had contained a sizable number of [[Sith (species)/Legends|pureblood Sith]], of whom only fifty-seven remained when the Sith made it out of the [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]]. By [[4985 BBY]], twelve had [[Death/Legends|died]] due to general misfortune, and no pureblood Sith [[Youngling/Legends|children]] had survived more than a [[Standard day/Legends|day]]. Meanwhile, the [[Human/Legends|Human]] population of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] flourished. The most prominent member of the purebloods on Kesh was [[Ravilan Wroth]], who often represented his compatriots in front of Lost Tribe leader [[Yaru Korsin]].<ref name="paragon" />

However, Wroth had his own gripe with the Lost Tribe, as he wanted Korsin to withdraw his people from Keshiri affairs and focus on finding a way off Kesh. To that end, Wroth came up with a plan&mdash;on a research trip to the [[Ragnos Lakes]] region, Wroth decided to [[Poison/Legends|poison]] the [[Water/Legends|water]] supply of the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tetsubal]] in order to create the appearance of a deadly virus ravaging the planet. Wroth successfully carried out his plan, using the compound [[cyanogen silicate]] to kill all 18,000 Keshiri residents of Tetsubal. However, his plan was discovered by Yaru Korsin's [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], who, already holding a prejudice against the purebloods, decided to frame Wroth for further crimes. Korsin performed the same deadly deed on seven other towns near Tetsubal, killing hundreds of thousands of Keshiri. Seelah was able to present her husband with the information that Wroth and his retinue had visited all those towns in recent days, as well as evidence that he had access to cyanogen silicate. Convinced of Wroth's complicity in the deaths, Korsin proclaimed that it was time for the [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]] members of the Lost Tribe to be [[Speciecide|eliminated]].<ref name="paragon" />

==The purge==
{{Quote|All gone. Right?''"<br />"''All gone. You are the last.|A captured Ravilan Wroth and Seelah Korsin, in the midst of the purge|<ref name="paragon" />}}
In a single night, all of the "Fifty-seven," as the non-Human Sith of Kesh were known&mdash;except for the [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] [[Gloyd]], a close friend of Yaru Korsin&mdash;were killed. The Fifty-seven did not go quietly, fighting the Lost Tribe [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] throughout the darkness in the mountains, though they could not withstand the attack for long. A young [[Unidentified sentry|sentry]] was trapped and killed, never abandoning his post until the bitter end. Another prominent member of the Fifty-seven, the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] translator [[Hestus]], was personally brought down by Seelah Korsin herself. The dead were beheaded and put on display in a plaza in the city of [[Tahv]], even while the remnants of the Fifty-seven still held out against Yaru Korsin and his chief [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]]. The final living members of the Fifty-seven were driven to a last stand high in the Takara Mountains, close to the ''Omen''{{'s}} original crash site. No quarter was given, and Yaru Korsin threw any who surrendered over the side of a cliff. Meanwhile, the wounded Ravilan Wroth was brought to the plaza where those already killed were displayed. Confronted by Seelah Korsin, Wroth admitted his complicity in the deaths at Tetsubal, but not in any of the other cities. Revealing her deception, Seelah took credit for those deaths, as well as the deaths of all the infant pureblood Sith who had been [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on Kesh since the ''Omen''{{'s}} crash, saying that Wroth and his people would have done the same to Seelah and her kind eventually. With that, [[Jariad Korsin]], Seelah's son, emerged from the darkness and killed Wroth, completing the purge.<ref name="paragon" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Seelah has done us a favor, reducing their numbers. She may do more.|Adari Vaal|<ref name="paragon" />}}
With that, all of the non-Human crewmembers of the ''Omen'', save Gloyd&mdash;<ref name="paragon" /> who himself would perish along with Yaru Korsin in a [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|lightsaber duel]] [[4975 BBY|ten years later]]&mdash;were killed.<ref name="savior">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior]]''</ref> Little did the Lost Tribe know that their purge was secretly supported by a [[Keshiri resistance]] movement dedicated to overthrowing Sith rule on Kesh. [[Tilden Kaah]], a secret operative of the resistance movement and the personal attendant to Seelah Korsin, brought the news to resistance leader [[Adari Vaal]] immediately after the purge's completion.<ref name="paragon" /> Although the Lost Tribe suffered a population loss due to the purge, it was more than made up for by a rapid increase in births over the next decade. In the years following the [[Blood/Legends|bloodshed]] of the purge, Yaru Korsin looked on the purge as an unfortunate but ultimately necessary event, as a homogenous Lost Tribe was easier to rule.<ref name="savior" /> Little knowledge of the Fifty-seven or the purge survived for very long, as Seelah Korsin took steps to erase them from history. Still, Keshiri tales spoke of "deformed" crewmembers of the ''Omen'' and their elimination. In fact, by [[3000 BBY]], there was an active [[Politics/Legends|political]] faction on Kesh known as [[Force 57]] that was comprised of physically imperfect members of the Lost Tribe, who revered Ravilan Wroth and the original Fifty-seven.<ref name="pantheon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The purge of the Fifty-seven first appeared in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[2010]] [[eBook]], ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''.<ref name="paragon" /> The event was also mentioned in two subsequent sequels, [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior|''Savior'']]<ref name="savior" /> and [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon|''Pantheon'']],<ref name="pantheon" /> along with the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.<ref name="erc">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> In his production notes for ''Paragon'', Miller revealed that he used the purge as a "story springboard" to move the Lost Tribe from its more diverse form seen in the Sith of the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series to the homogenous kind found in the later [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] novels.<ref name="paragonjjm">{{Faraway|url=fiction/ebooks/sw-losttribeofthesith3.html|text=Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith Part 3: Paragon}}</ref>
